- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for rebound.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior), true outcome often corrects downward within 3–5 days; apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to subsequent forecasts.  
- Model consistently underestimates in periods with high historical volatility (e.g., 3+ consecutive price jumps); add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to neutral/negative), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply a 2–5% smoothing filter to reduce overreaction to short-term sentiment spikes.
